faq.a: Shadi is associated with the Arabic form شَادِي, whose core sense is shadi; singer.

faq.q: What is the origin of Shadi?
faq.a: Shadi is associated with Arabic. Shadi is Arabic شَادِي (Shādī), the active participle of شَدَا, meaning 'singer'.
Yes — the underlying form شَادِي is Arabic.
Shadi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shadi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shādī is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shadi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Shadi is rendered شادی and carries the sense شادی، گانے والا.

faq.q: What does Shadi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shadi is rendered شادی and carries the sense شادی، خواننده.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shadi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shadi, shadi. Script forms are شادي, شادی, شَادِي, शादी.

faq.q: Is Shadi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
